title: The scale, fixed
spoken: The Lorentz factor is one over the square root of one minus v squared over c squared.
explanation: Going to the moving system and back must return every event unchanged, and the scale must not depend on the direction of motion or jump at v = 0. Those three conditions fix the factor as this.
assumptions: The moving system k moves along the x axis of the stationary system K at speed v, with |v| < c, and the two origins coincide at time zero.
Modern teaching notation. The paper writes the moving system's coordinates as xi and tau, not x′ and t′, its gamma as beta, and the speed of light as V.
The unknown factor is the same for v and −v (no direction in space is special) and equals 1 at v = 0.

notes.title: One over it
notes.explanation: Dividing 1 by a number below 1 gives a number above 1. At v = 0.6c the root is 0.8 and the factor 1.25.

notes.title: c squared
notes.explanation: The square of the speed of light.

notes.title: Its square root
notes.explanation: The positive root, so that the factor is 1 at rest.

notes.title: One minus that
notes.explanation: Positive for every speed below c, zero at c, so no system moves at c.

notes.title: How close to light speed
notes.explanation: v squared over c squared is 0 at rest and approaches 1 as v approaches c.

notes.title: What it defines
notes.explanation: The value of the common factor. From here on the transformation has no unknowns.

notes.title: v squared
notes.explanation: Squaring removes the direction: moving either way gives the same factor.

notes.title: Lorentz factor
notes.explanation: One over the square root of one minus v squared over c squared: 1 at rest, larger at any speed, without limit as v approaches c. The paper writes it as beta.

notes.title: Speed of light
notes.explanation: The paper's V. It enters because both systems must find the same speed for light.

notes.title: Speed of the moving system
notes.explanation: The speed of k relative to K. Its sign gives the direction.
